listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, October 24. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is from Sudan. Drop Site News reports that a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region killed more than 150 people. The report describes it as part of a wave of large scale attacks by the Sudanese army. The figures come from one outlet, so treat them with care. Now the front page. In the NBA, Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama's game-tying layup with less than a second left. The Rockets beat the Spurs 114 to 110 and are now 2 and 0. In the NFL, the 49ers have ruled out receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, and defensive end Nick Bosa, for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Receiver Christian Kirk may return. At Anthropic, the company is committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. Its structure increases the stake as the company grows. In space, NASA says Artemis Three will launch in 2027. It will test future Moon lander operations before astronauts return to the lunar surface. Now the sections. In tech, a new Claude API version dated October 21 is out, with new SDK releases. Anthropic is also expanding its Cyber Verification Program for qualifying security professionals. And Cloudflare's security audit skill is trending on GitHub. In politics, a congressional watchdog report says some Pentagon AI projects do not always follow the agency's own guidelines. NPR says Ohio could decide Senate control, with rural voters key. Drop Site's daily briefing covers a West Bank lockdown and Brent crude at 114 dollars. In world news, Ukraine and Russia have confirmed a truce in the occupied city of Oleshky. Authorities are investigating whether the first Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths. And France is preparing for a day of protest, with more than 70,000 police officers to be deployed. In sports, ESPN previews the third fight between Yan and Dvalishvili. Matt Olson of the Braves won his sixth Fielding Bible Award. In Atlanta, a letter to the editor weighs in on the proposed Beltline rail project. The city's first bike park is nearly finished on the Westside. And a vote on demolishing the home where Michael Hardwick was arrested in 1982 has been delayed until November. In architecture, ArchDaily features Álvaro Siza Vieira's Colien House. AEC Magazine looks at what comes after automated drawings. And VAILLO and Architects renovated the Basque Museum in Bilbao. In science, NASA's Swift Observatory has ended its science mission. Researchers suggest an ancient virus may have shaped chimp brain evolution. And in Poland, scientists say wetlands could act as natural defences for an ancient forest. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Sudanese Army Drone Strikes Kill Scores of Civilians in Crowded Market
lead.note: A drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region of Sudan killed more than 150 people, according to Drop Site News. The report describes the strike as part of a wave of large scale attacks by the Sudanese army. Its headline says the strikes killed scores of civilians in a crowded market. The strike took place in Abyei, a region described in the report as disputed. The summary gives no further detail on the victims, the timing or any response, so those points are not yet clear from this item. For a reader following world news, it is a report of high civilian casualties that deserves attention today. Readers should treat the figures as those given by one outlet until other sources confirm them.
